assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1997 localisation of gamma-ray burst counterparts settled a thirty-year puzzle: bursts are cosmological, and the afterglow opened a multiwavelength window on the most energetic explosions and, later, on compact-object mergers. This is an observational result enabled by an instrument (the BeppoSAX wide-field and narrow-field X-ray cameras), which is the kind of work I value most.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX discovery of the X-ray afterglow and the rapid localisations; Kulkarni's group secured the optical, radio and redshift follow-up that fixed the distance scale. The supplied credit supports a fair three-person configuration, but I recall other decisive contributors (optical counterpart and spectroscopy teams, and the afterglow theorists) that this three-name credit leaves out, so some allocation is arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: nearly three decades of independent confirmation by Swift, Fermi and ground facilities, and the interpretation (relativistic blast waves, collapsar and merger origins) is stable. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Who among the BeppoSAX team, the optical discoverers and the theorists is decisive is contested; a three-person limit forces exclusions.
I am recalling the history from memory and have not independently verified individual roles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength idea, brought fractional uncertainty to the 10^-18 level and now underpins tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and the prospect of a redefinition of the second. It is a precision-measurement achievement with clear originality and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clock; Ye drove the systematic accuracy and stability records. The two-name credit is a clean allocation, although Hall and Hansch were already honoured in 2005 for the frequency comb that makes the clocks possible, and ion-clock pioneers are outside this credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: several independent laboratories (Sr, Yb) reproduce and improve the performance, and international comparisons are routine. Timing is good, with the redefinition of the second still pending.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 prize for the comb and the 2012 prize for ion control may weigh against it with some colleagues.
The relative claim of lattice clocks versus single-ion clocks for the foundational credit is not settled by the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in 2013, then the blazar TXS 0506+056 association (2018) and the Galactic-plane neutrino emission (2023), established neutrino astronomy. The instrument, a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice instrumented with photomultipliers, is a remarkable detector achievement.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA, so he is the natural single laureate in the supplied credit. A full allocation might also recognise the early detector pioneers and the 2013 analysis leaders, but none appears in the exact credited names, so I propose only Halzen.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature as an observatory result: the diffuse flux is firmly established and cross-checked by ANTARES and Baikal-GVD. The source identification remains thinner, with one high-significance source and the Galactic plane, so some would say it is a few years early.
uncertainties: Origin of most of the diffuse flux is still unresolved.
Whether a single-person award fairly reflects a collaboration of about 350 people and earlier pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a new class of materials with protected edge and surface states, with first-rate theory followed by a decisive transport experiment. The impact on condensed-matter physics has been very large. This lies outside my own expertise, so I weight the view of colleagues from that area.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 topological invariant and the quantum spin Hall effect in graphene; Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe quantum wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The supplied three-name credit is coherent, but Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and the early 3D-material experimentalists, are not among the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent confirmations in HgTe, InAs/GaSb and Bi-based 3D materials with ARPES. Timing is good, though the 2016 prize touched topological phases.
uncertainties: Competing claims of Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents leave the theory credit open.
Partial overlap with the 2016 topological-phase prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of baryon acoustic oscillations in the galaxy distribution in 2005 gave cosmology a calibrated standard ruler, now central to measuring dark-energy evolution and the Hubble tension. It is a clear, observationally driven discovery that depends on large survey instruments.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein (SDSS luminous red galaxies) and Cole, Percival (2dFGRS) reported near-simultaneous detections, which supports a fair three-person grouping. The theoretical prediction credit (Peebles, Yu; Sunyaev, Zeldovich) is outside the list and may need to be considered.
assessment.maturity: Mature and confirmed by BOSS, WiggleZ, eBOSS and DESI, with a stable interpretation. Recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy are still uncertain and do not affect the discovery itself.
uncertainties: Credit may be split between prediction and detection.
Survey collaborations are large and the leading contributors are partly a matter of judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC completed the Standard Model; the detector and trigger engineering behind ATLAS and CMS was extraordinary, and the discovery is a landmark. The theory was already recognised in 2013, so the question here is whether detector and collaboration leadership merits a separate prize.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are the founding leaders of the CMS and ATLAS projects, so the credit is a defensible but leadership-based allocation; analysis-level contributors and the accelerator builders are not included. Such an award would clash with the traditional emphasis on specific individual contributions.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed, with couplings measured to growing precision. Timing is not premature, but it is late and the 2013 prize has partly addressed the physics.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wishes to honour experimental leadership after the 2013 theory prize.
The strict three-person limit versus thousands of collaborators.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of magic angles and the 2018 discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials as a tunable platform, with a rapidly expanding field. The combination of a clear prediction and a prompt experimental confirmation is attractive. I defer to condensed-matter colleagues.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experiments. Others, notably Cory Dean's hBN-encapsulated devices and Pablo's co-workers, would be argued for, but only the supplied names can be proposed.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in many laboratories, although the superconducting pairing mechanism and the many competing phases are not settled. The discovery is only about eight years old and may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and some reproducibility of device-dependent phases remain open.
Disputed credit between theory and several experimental groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised controllable many-body Hamiltonians (superfluid-to-Mott transition, quantum gas microscopes) that serve as quantum simulators. The conceptual and technical impact is significant, but the field is in my colleagues' domain and the claim of a single discovery is diffuse.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch-Zoller proposal and the Greiner-Bloch Mott-insulator experiment are the central items; Cirac, also on the credit, is a natural theory co-contributor but cannot be added to a three-person limit without removing someone. The configuration is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a technique, with many groups reproducing the experiments, but the quantum-simulation promise for open problems is still evolving.
uncertainties: Overlap with the BEC prize (2001), the 2012 prize for quantum optics and the 2025 prize.
Choice between a theory-led and an experiment-led trio is not clearly decided by the supplied text.
